conceptZh: 沒電的小玩具機器人整個垮下來，手臂軟趴趴；一顆胖電池自己滾過來喀一聲插進他背後，他瞬間彈直、跳起一段超級浮誇的機器人舞，然後再度沒電垮掉。
object: a small toy robot and a chunky cartoon battery
morph: the glyph 電 stands still as a solid sculpture while the recharging gag plays out at its base
creativeAngle: 機器人主題的核心：用「沒電垮掉→充電暴走跳舞→又沒電」的三拍節奏做笑點，因果非常好懂。電上為雨部、下為电，筆畫多且雨部四點常被畫糊，所以讓字體靜止。語音詞「電池」，電ㄉㄧㄢˋ、池ㄔˊ都是單一讀音，且雨部孩子已經學過。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale butter cream background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 電 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep royal blue, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the 雨 radical on top, with its four inner dots clearly separated, sits above the 电 component whose bottom stroke hooks upward. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. At its base slumps a small boxy toy robot, completely out of power: knees folded, arms hanging like wet noodles, visor dim and drooping. From 0.6 to 1.8 seconds nothing happens except one arm slowly sliding further down, which is the joke. At 2.0 seconds a chunky cartoon battery, almost as big as he is, rolls in from the left, bumps his heel, wobbles upright and clicks into a socket on his back. His visor snaps bright, he springs bolt upright, and from 2.6 to 4.0 seconds he performs an absurdly over-committed robot dance on the spot - stiff elbows, spinning head, a little hip shimmy - far more energy than the moment needs. At 4.1 seconds the battery pops back out, and he droops instantly back into the exact same puddle pose as the start, one arm still raised mid-dance. He and the battery slide out of frame to the left by 4.7 seconds. From 4.8 to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 電 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「電、電、電池」, using the reading ㄉㄧㄢˋ for 電 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 電 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 電池 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 電: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 電讓電風扇轉動；發條樂團想吹風耍帥，卻被風吹出一連串走音與翻倒。
object: An original wind-up animal trio with cymbals, a squeeze-bulb horn and a drum, plus one small electric fan.
morph: The complete glyph remains a stationary, solid-colored teaching sculpture; an electric fan demonstrates its meaning through the band's physical comedy.
creativeAngle: 改用電風扇引發樂器連環失控，取代電池充電笑點。自信的發條樂團先被風吹得敲錯、吹錯、翻倒，再調低風速成功合奏；字形全程完整，不拿筆畫當道具。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation in one locked, front-facing shot. Center one correctly formed Traditional Chinese glyph 電, occupying about 70% of frame height with comfortable margins. Use a standard Taiwanese textbook glyph as the exact silhouette: clearly separated dots in the upper 雨 component and a fully legible lower portion with its turning hook. Render every stroke in solid saturated cobalt blue against a pale peach background, with soft studio lighting. The complete glyph is present from the first frame and stays stationary, unobstructed and uncropped throughout.

Along the lower foreground, safely below the glyph, stage an original miniature wind-up animal band: a bossy wooden duck cymbal player, an earnest wooden mouse with a squeeze-bulb horn, and a round wooden bear drummer. Visible brass winding keys establish their mechanical toy identity. Their instruments belong to the band; the only additional object is a small electric fan with a guarded rotor, an integrated speed lever and a short power cord leading offscreen along the floor. Keep these miniature objects clearly separated from the character's strokes.

At the opening, the duck confidently raises its cymbals and gestures for a grand entrance. At 0.8 seconds it nudges the fan's speed lever with its foot, expecting a glamorous breeze. The electrically powered rotor accelerates smoothly; the trio proudly lean into the airflow for a brief anticipation beat. From 1.5 to 3.1 seconds, deliver one readable domino mishap: the breeze tips the duck's raised cymbals together with a soft clash; its backward wobble presses the mouse's horn bulb for a ridiculous little honk; the mouse's horn bell nudges the bear's drum, which tips onto its side and gently rolls the round bear backward onto its bottom. Show each contact distinctly. The duck freezes with an astonished open beak while the bear calmly taps the sideways drum once. No sparks or flashing light.

From 3.2 to 4.6 seconds, the duck sheepishly lowers the fan speed, the bear rights its drum, and the trio successfully play one tiny coordinated flourish, then bow. Their winding keys continue turning independently of the electric fan, making the distinction clear. By 4.8 seconds all action has settled. Hold the centered 電 completely clear and still through 8.0 seconds; the band rests quietly below it and the fan rotor stops smoothly. Use bright painted wood, rounded forms and expressive toy faces, with an uncluttered composition and no camera movement.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「電、電、電風扇」. Say the first 電 at approximately 0.2 seconds, the second at 1.0 seconds, and 電風扇 naturally between 5.3 and 6.5 seconds while the glyph is clearly held. Use ㄉㄧㄢˋ consistently. Stop speaking after the word. Keep the clash, honk, drum tap and fan hum gentle and below the voice; use no background music. The vocabulary is audio only. The single glyph 電 is the only on-screen writing: no subtitles, labels, other characters, logos or watermarks.
